solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique, linked answer split by the grid); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Doctor here treats lucratively, first and last

definitions.text: Doctor here treats lucratively, first and last

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters that follow are rearranged
only the opening and closing letters of the preceding word are kept, the rest discarded

blocks.note: taken as written
the opening and closing letters of this word

explanation.surface: A doctor in this place makes good money from treatments.
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue is both wordplay and definition: HARLEY STREET in London is famous for expensive private medical practices.
explanation.definitionFit: The London street is lined with private consultants' rooms, where wealthy patients pay high fees for treatment.

clue.text: Leave Native American forest at last

indicators.note: at last points to the final letter of the word it follows

blocks.note: the Hopi are a Native American people of Arizona
the final letter of this word

explanation.surface: Someone is told to depart from a Native American woodland at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Hop it is a British slang command meaning go away, so it works as an imperative to depart.

clue.text: Rifle fire controlled to begin with

indicators.note: says the word just before it is placed at the start, ahead of the other part

blocks.note: to run a business is to control it
to fire someone is to sack them

explanation.surface: A rifle is fired under control at first, like a shooting range instruction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Rifle' and 'fire' both suggest guns; here rifle is a verb meaning search roughly.
explanation.definitionFit: To rifle through a place is to search it thoroughly and roughly, often stealing, which is what ransacking means.

clue.text: Being sixteen upset the established church

indicators.note: something upset is knocked out of order, so its letters are rearranged

blocks.note: taken as written
CE is the Church of England, the established church

explanation.surface: A sixteen-year-old is upset with the Church of England.
explanation.definitionFit: Being as a noun is the state of existing, a direct synonym.

clue.text: See 1
Sharp point in the centre of muntjac antler

indicators.note: points to the single letter at the middle of the next word

blocks.note: the fourth of seven letters sits at the centre
an antler is a deer's horn

explanation.surface: A muntjac deer's antler ends in a sharp point.
explanation.walkthrough: A muntjac is a small deer, so the surface reads naturally about its antler tip.
explanation.definitionFit: A thorn is a sharp spike on a plant stem, a natural pointed tip.

clue.text: A setter after cheese and beans

indicators.note: after places the words before it behind the word that follows

blocks.note: Edam is a Dutch cheese
taken as written
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: The crossword setter goes for cheese and beans, perhaps on toast.
explanation.definitionFit: Edamame are young green soybeans served in the pod, a Japanese dish.

clue.text: See 13
Endless ropes for sailors in budget carrier outdoors

indicators.note: with no ends, the word loses both its first and last letters
one thing in place of another, so one group of letters swaps out the other

blocks.note: the word with its outer letters removed
RYA is the Royal Yachting Association, a body of sailors
Ryanair is a low-cost airline

explanation.surface: Sailors' ropes are stowed aboard a cheap airline flight.
explanation.walkthrough: In RYANAIR, the RYA is replaced by OPE, leaving OPEN AIR. Ryanair is an Irish budget airline.
explanation.definitionFit: Something open-air takes place outside rather than under a roof, so it happens outdoors.

clue.text: Go ahead and place a bet, lady

blocks.note: as in 'do it', proceed
to wager is to bet

explanation.surface: Someone urges a lady to go ahead and gamble.
explanation.definitionFit: A dowager is a widow holding a title from her late husband, hence a dignified elderly lady.

clue.text: Volume of fizzy drink heard in dream

indicators.note: heard means the words are taken by their spoken sound, not spelling

blocks.note: Fanta is an orange fizzy drink and size is volume

explanation.surface: The size of a can of soda is overheard during a dream.
explanation.definitionFit: To fantasise is to daydream, imagining things that are wished for.

clue.text: Transport crew overwhelmed by stress

indicators.note: being overwhelmed means being swamped and surrounded by something else

blocks.note: strain is stress
a crew is a team

explanation.surface: Transport workers are swamped by pressure at work.
explanation.definitionFit: A steam train is a railway engine powered by steam, a means of transport.

clue.text: Sharp as a group of police officers

blocks.note: taken as written
CID is the Criminal Investigation Department, British plain-clothes detectives

explanation.surface: A team of detectives is said to be sharp-witted.
explanation.definitionFit: Acid as an adjective describes a sharp, biting taste or tone of remark.

clue.text: Come round socially aware by the first of November

indicators.note: keeps only the opening letter of the word that follows

blocks.note: woke is slang for alert to social injustice
the opening letter of the month

explanation.surface: Someone becomes politically conscious by early November.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition reads as a past participle: having come round from sleep is having woken.
explanation.definitionFit: To come round is to regain consciousness, which is to have woken up.

clue.text: Disappeared as a result of defenestration

blocks.note: first meaning: the idiom for something lost or abandoned
second meaning: literally, what happens to someone thrown through a window

explanation.walkthrough: Defenestration is the act of throwing someone out of a window, so the second half is the idiom taken literally.
explanation.definitionFit: The idiom means vanished or was abandoned completely, as hopes or plans do when they are lost.

clue.text: Divers risk finding neglected sides in old city

indicators.note: sides are the edges, so only the outermost letters of the word are kept
in places those letters inside the following word

blocks.note: Thebes is an ancient city of Egypt and of Greece
the first and last letters of this word

explanation.surface: Divers in an ancient city run the risk of being ignored.
explanation.definitionFit: Decompression sickness, which strikes divers who surface too fast, is commonly called this.

clue.text: Will manager report scams with previous old money?

indicators.note: a report is something spoken, so the word is taken by its sound

blocks.note: ex means former
the ecu was the European Currency Unit, before the euro
scams are tricks

explanation.surface: A report on frauds involving former currency asks who manages things.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Will' is not a name or a verb but a legal document.
explanation.definitionFit: An executrix is a woman appointed to carry out the terms of someone's will after death.

clue.text: Footwear, half-sandal, reeks awfully

indicators.note: half means only one portion of the word is kept, the rest dropped
something done awfully is done badly, so the letters come out disordered

blocks.note: the first three of the six letters
taken as written

explanation.surface: Someone's shoes, half sandals, smell terrible.
explanation.definitionFit: Sneakers are soft rubber-soled sports shoes, so they are a kind of footwear.

clue.text: Theoretical monk in the middle of the road

indicators.note: the first item is set inside the second, sitting at its centre

blocks.note: the A1 is Britain's longest numbered road, written AI with the digit as a letter
a prior is a monk heading a priory

explanation.surface: A monk stands in the middle of the road, thinking abstractly.
explanation.definitionFit: A priori reasoning works from principles rather than observed experience, so it is theoretical.

clue.text: Joint that should be distinguishable from the rear

definitions.text: Joint that should be distinguishable from the rear

blocks.clueFragment: Joint that should be distinguishable from the rear
blocks.note: surface: a joint at the back of the body that must not be confused with another
setter's reading: the insult about someone who does not know his arse from this arm joint

explanation.walkthrough: It plays on the saying that an incompetent person does not know their arse from their elbow; the rear is the arse.
explanation.definitionFit: The arm joint between upper arm and forearm is the one in the rude saying about incompetence.

clue.text: Flier 'behaved as expected', said complaint

indicators.note: said means the words are taken as spoken, by their sound

blocks.note: a flier is a bird, and doing what is expected of one is that it flew

explanation.surface: A pilot reportedly behaved properly, says the complaint.
explanation.definitionFit: Complaint here means an illness, and avian influenza is a disease.

clue.text: Sounds like the FT's time

indicators.note: this directly announces that a spoken sound gives the answer

blocks.note: the FT setter, writing in the Financial Times, calls the paper's things ours

explanation.surface: A chime that resembles the Financial Times clock.
explanation.definitionFit: An hour is a unit of time, sixty minutes.

clue.text: Pretence contrived about square dance

indicators.note: letters made to dance move about and land in a new order
about means going around, so one word wraps the other

blocks.note: something contrived is made up
taken as written

explanation.surface: A contrived act centred on a square dance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square dance' looks like one phrase, a folk dance; split it, and dance is the anagram signal.
explanation.definitionFit: A masquerade is a false show or disguise, so it is a pretence.

clue.text: Signifies wealth

blocks.note: first meaning: a verb, to indicate or denote
second meaning: a noun, money or resources

explanation.walkthrough: Two separate senses of one word: a verb and a plural noun.
explanation.definitionFit: A word that means something is said to denote it, and a person of private income has independent resources.

clue.text: Lament turning in the griddle

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the run of words that follows
turning round means the letters are read the other way

blocks.note: letters spanning the two words

explanation.surface: Someone moans while turning food on the griddle.
explanation.definitionFit: A dirge is a mournful song for the dead, a musical lament.

clue.text: German guy and Turkish guy in bed

blocks.note: Otto is a typical German man's name
a guy is a man; the Turkish adds a nod to the whole word's other sense

explanation.surface: Two men, one German and one Turkish, are sharing a bed.
explanation.walkthrough: The answer also means a Turk of the old empire, so 'Turkish guy' doubles as a hint to the whole.
explanation.definitionFit: An ottoman is an upholstered seat or storage bed, a padded piece of furniture.

clue.text: Rat music, for example

blocks.note: surface: a music genre that sounds like something rodents would play
setter's reading: these three letters are a rearranged form of a word for creative work

explanation.walkthrough: The answer read as two words describes 'Rat': it is a re-formed version of the word for creativity.
explanation.definitionFit: Music is one category of creative expression, alongside painting and literature.

clue.text: Disturbing sexy film lines recited for no good reason

indicators.note: disturbing things knocks them out of place, so the letters are rearranged
recited means spoken aloud, so the sound gives the spelling

blocks.note: taken as written
an actor's cues are the lines that prompt them

explanation.surface: A racy movie upsets people as its dialogue is spoken without justification.
explanation.definitionFit: A weak, unconvincing justification is no good reason at all.
